explanations: terra: The Book opens as guidance ("هُدًۭى") for those who guard themselves, the textual companion of the road-prayer.

luna: The mindful are already described as being upon guidance from their Lord (هُدًى), the grounded state of those who find the way. | terra: The guarded stand upon guidance from their Lord ("عَلَىٰ هُدًۭى"), a stable position rather than a merely known direction.

luna: Those who trade guidance for error make a losing exchange (اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى), choosing the wrong route after seeing both. | terra: They buy error in exchange for guidance, making guidance something abandoned for a contrary course.
terra: The first public command is to worship the Lord who created people and those before them, making worship the ground of God-consciousness.
terra: God makes the earth a resting-bed, the sky a canopy, and water a source of provision, preparing the ground where people live and move.

luna: God guides many by a parable and leaves many astray through it; only the defiantly disobedient are left to their error. | terra: The same parabolic sign misleads many and guides many, showing that a sign does not guide apart from its receiver.
luna: Those who break God's covenant and sever what He commanded to be joined are named losers, the communal fragmentation opposed to a worn shared path.

luna: God promises that when guidance (هُدًى) comes from Him, whoever follows it will have no fear or grief. | terra: When guidance comes from God, those who follow it have neither fear nor grief: the traveller's instruction is to follow.
luna: Those who reject the signs and deny them are companions of the Fire, the contrary end to following guidance.

luna: God parts the sea for the Children of Israel, saves them, and drowns Pharaoh's people, a collective passage out of danger. | terra: The sea is parted for Israel, saving them and drowning Pharaoh's people before their eyes: a route is made where none appeared.
terra: Israel's covenant begins with worshipping God alone and then gives a social path of good speech, prayer, alms, and care for kin and the needy.
terra: Gabriel brings down the confirming Book as guidance and good news for believers.
terra: Exchanging faith for disbelief is explicitly called losing the even road, "ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ".
terra: "إِنَّ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ هُوَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ" makes God's own guidance the measure against rival communal directions.
terra: After Abraham is tested and fulfils the words, God makes him an "إِمَامًا" for the people: a proved walker becomes a guide in front.
terra: The House is made a place of return and safety, giving the shown destination a place where walkers return.
terra: Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations, the destination around which the later route is gathered.
terra: Abraham asks for a submitting community and for God to show them their rites, a communal practice learned on the way to the House.
terra: The answer to competing inherited identities is Abraham's upright religion ("مِلَّةَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفًۭا").

luna: God guides whom He wills to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), answering the question of direction in the qibla passage. | terra: In the contested change of direction, God guides whom He wills to a straight road; orientation is both bodily and communal.

luna: The community is made a middle nation (أُمَّةً وَسَطًا), with its direction tested through following the Messenger. | terra: The believers are made a middle community ("أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا") to bear witness, while the qiblah test distinguishes those who follow the messenger.
terra: God turns the Prophet toward a qiblah that pleases him and commands faces toward the Sacred Mosque: guidance receives a bodily direction.
terra: People of Scripture will not follow the Prophet's qiblah, nor will he follow theirs; competing directions are made irreconcilable.
terra: From wherever the traveller goes out, he is commanded to turn his face toward the Sacred Mosque.
terra: The qiblah instruction completes God's favour and ends "لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ", joining bodily direction to favour and guidance.

luna: Safa and Marwa are among God's symbols (شَعَائِرِ اللَّه); pilgrims go between them, leaving a repeated path of seeking and remembrance. | terra: Ṣafā and Marwah are God's "شَعَآئِر"; traversing between two visible signs turns a route to the House into worship.

luna: People refuse revelation and follow inherited footsteps instead (نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا), even when those before them lacked guidance. | terra: Those summoned to revelation answer that they follow what they found their fathers upon, an ancestral track without guidance.
terra: They purchase error for guidance and punishment for forgiveness, making the road a deliberately traded good.
terra: The Qur'an is sent as guidance for people and clear discriminations, a public marker for the way.
luna: The instruction to enter houses by their doors (وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا) makes finding the right entrance a small image of reaching the home by its proper way.
terra: The pilgrimage and lesser pilgrimage are completed for God; blocked travellers make an offering, showing a route interrupted yet still worshipfully held.
terra: Pilgrimage has known months, forbids quarrel and sexual disorder, and calls the traveller to provision whose best form is God-consciousness.
terra: On the pilgrimage route, departure from ʿArafāt reaches the Sacred Landmark ("ٱلْمَشْعَرِ ٱلْحَرَام") and remembers God who guided the travellers after they had been astray.
terra: Pilgrims are commanded to depart from where all people depart and seek forgiveness, keeping the route shared rather than privately invented.
luna: Believers are told to enter submission wholly and not follow Satan's footsteps (خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَان), a contrary trail laid for walkers.

luna: Humanity begins as one community, then disputes; prophets and Scripture guide the people to truth (يَهْدِي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا), preserving unity and divergence. | terra: After people become divided, God guides believers to the truth they disputed, and He guides whom He wills to a straight road.
terra: Barring people from God's way and the Sacred Mosque is counted a grave obstruction, while the road to the House is at stake.

luna: Whoever rejects false gods and believes in God has grasped the firm handhold (الْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَىٰ) that cannot break, an image of a secure route. | terra: Right direction is made distinct from error ("ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىِّ"), the boundary a walker must recognize.

luna: God brings believers from darkness into light, while false patrons lead others back into darkness: two opposed routes and guides. | terra: God brings believers from darkness into light, while false powers bring their companions from light into darkness.
terra: The Prophet is told that their guidance is not incumbent on him; God guides whom He wills, clarifying the guide's limit.
terra: Here "تَضِلَّ" means that one witness forgets or errs and another reminds her, a non-travel sense of the root that keeps lostness from being reduced to geography.

luna: The prayer asks God not to let hearts deviate after guidance (لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا), a plea to stay on the route. | terra: Those given guidance ask, "do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us," treating continuance on the road as a gift.
terra: The religion with God is submission, setting one divine dīn beneath the many competing communal courses.
terra: God as "مَٰلِكَ ٱلْمُلْك" has sovereignty rather than the road-middle sense heard beside "مَٰلِك" in Fātiḥah; ownership governs every route.
terra: "فَٱتَّبِعُونِ" makes following the messenger the route by which God loves and forgives the hearers.

luna: Jesus says God is his Lord and theirs, so worship Him; this is a straight path (صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ). | terra: Jesus says worship the Lord of both speaker and hearers; "هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ".
terra: Those nearest Abraham are those who followed him, this Prophet, and the believers: affinity is walking after a predecessor.
terra: The passage insists that guidance is God's guidance, even where human groups attempt to monopolize it.
terra: A religion other than submission is not accepted, marking an ultimate boundary between courses.
terra: How can a people be guided after rejecting faith once its truth and the messenger's witness have reached them?
terra: Believers are commanded to follow Abraham's upright religion, an earlier line of travel.

luna: The first House is established for people, blessed and a guidance for all worlds (هُدًى لِّلْعَالَمِينَ), the home toward which the path leads. | terra: The first House is blessed and "هُدًۭى لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ": the house named at the end of guidance is itself a guide for the worlds.

luna: The House contains clear signs and Abraham's station; pilgrimage to it is due for those able, completing the route to a known destination. | terra: The House contains clear "ءَايَٰت", gives security to the arrival, and makes pilgrimage incumbent on whoever can find a "سَبِيلًا" to it.
terra: People of Scripture are challenged for barring believers from God's way and seeking crookedness ("عِوَجًۭا") in it.
terra: Holding fast to God ("يَعْتَصِمۢ بِٱللَّه") is described as being guided to a straight road.
luna: Believers are told to fear God as He deserves and remain wholly submitted until death, a sustained course of devotion.

luna: The community is told to hold fast together to God's rope and not divide (وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا), keeping many walkers on one shared course. | terra: Holding together to God's rope and not dividing turns former enmity into joined hearts, the social contrary to paths that scatter.

luna: A community is to call others to good, command right, and forbid wrong, acting as guides along the way. | terra: A community is to call to good, command what is right, and forbid wrong: a people can become a guiding body.
terra: Believers are warned not to become those who separated and differed after clear proofs came to them.
terra: The best community is marked by commanding right, forbidding wrong, and faith, the practices that keep a group oriented.
terra: This is a clear statement for people, and guidance and admonition for the God-conscious.
terra: Sending a messenger who recites signs, purifies, and teaches Book and wisdom is named a great divine favour to believers.
terra: Signs in the creation of heavens and earth invite orientation by reflection, though they are not literal road marks.
terra: God promises to show believers the "سُنَن" of those before them: guidance is a received, already-walked course.
terra: Worship God without associating anything with Him, then extend goodness through the concentric circle of neighbours and travellers.

luna: Some given a share of Scripture buy error and want others to stray from the way (السَّبِيل), choosing a route and inviting others onto it. | terra: Those who purchase error desire that believers too lose the way ("تَضِلُّوا۟ ٱلسَّبِيلَ").
terra: Those given Scripture call disbelievers better guided in way ("أَهْدَىٰ ... سَبِيلًۭا") than believers, a judgement whose direction is reversed.
terra: Satan wants to lead those who seek false judgement far into error ("ضَلَٰلًۢا بَعِيدًۭا").
luna: Had the people obeyed the instruction to leave home or fight, it would have been better and firmer for them; steadfastness follows submission.
luna: Obedience would bring a great reward from God, continuing the preceding promise of a firm route.

luna: Obedience to God and the Messenger is followed by guidance to a straight path (صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا), immediately before the description of the favored people. | terra: Obedience to God and messenger would bring the people to a straight road.

luna: Those who obey God and the Messenger join the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous whom God favored (أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ), naming the community whose path is sought. | terra: Obedience places a person with those God has favoured ("أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم"), identifying the human company behind the requested road.
luna: The favor described for those who obey God and the Messenger is bounty from God, completing the account of the favored company.
terra: Believers fight in God's way while disbelievers fight in the way of false powers; the two allegiances form opposed courses.
terra: Whomever God leaves astray, no way can be found for him ("فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُۥ سَبِيلًۭا").
terra: Angels ask those who wronged themselves why they did not migrate when God's earth was wide, setting the literal road behind 4:98.
terra: The weak, women, and children who can devise no plan and cannot find a way ("لَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًۭا") stage literal inability to leave.
terra: A group tries to lead the Prophet astray, but God reveals Book and wisdom and teaches him; divine favour counters false direction.

luna: One who opposes the Messenger and follows a way other than the believers' (سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) is left to that chosen route. | terra: Following other than the believers' way after guidance becomes clear leads away from their trodden communal course.
terra: Associating others with God is described as going far astray, a long departure from the course.
luna: Satan curses himself and claims he will take a share of God's servants, presenting a rival master for people to follow.
luna: Satan promises to command his followers to alter God's creation; taking him as patron is named a clear loss.
terra: The best religion belongs to one who submits to God, does good, and follows the upright religion of Abraham.
terra: Believers are commanded to stand firmly for justice ("قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ"), a moral use of steadfast uprightness.
terra: Disbelief in God, angels, books, messengers, and the Last Day is a far straying ("ضَلَٰلًۢا بَعِيدًۭا").
terra: Repeated turns between faith and disbelief end with God's refusal to forgive or guide to a way.
terra: Disbelief coupled with barring others from God's way is described as straying far away.
terra: Those who disbelieve and wrong cannot be forgiven or guided to a way.
terra: The withheld way is specified as the road of Hell ("طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ").
luna: Those who hold fast to God are guided to Him on a straight path (صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا). | terra: Those who believe and hold fast are brought into mercy and guided to God by a straight road.
terra: God explains the inheritance ruling "أَن تَضِلُّوا۟"—lest people err—another legal rather than spatial use of lostness.
terra: Sacred markers, offerings, garlands, and people intending the Sacred House in search of bounty and pleasure make pilgrimage a marked route.
terra: The religion is completed and favour perfected, giving "دِين" a completed communal form rather than only a habitual track.

luna: Believers must stand firm for justice (كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ) and not let hatred turn them aside; justice is nearer to mindfulness. | terra: Believers are commanded to stand firm for God as witnesses in justice, even against hatred.
luna: Keeping the covenant leads to pardon and gardens; disbelief after it is straying from the middle of the way (سَوَاءَ السَّبِيل).
luna: The Messenger brings light and a clarifying Book from God, preparing the next verse's account of guidance out of darkness.

luna: The Book guides those seeking God's approval to paths of peace (سُبُلَ السَّلَام), brings them from darkness to light, and guides them to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ). | terra: By the revelation God guides seekers of His pleasure to "سُبُلَ ٱلسَّلَٰم" and then to a straight road.
luna: Moses recalls God's favor (نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ) in appointing prophets, making kings, and giving blessings, before the community is told to enter the land.
luna: Moses commands his people to enter the holy land God assigned them and not turn back, a direct route offered to a favored community.
luna: The people refuse the land because powerful inhabitants are there, turning away from the route through fear.
luna: Two God-fearing men urge the people to enter through the gate and rely on God, a guide's counsel at the threshold.
luna: The people refuse to enter and tell Moses and God to go fight alone, choosing separation from the offered way.
luna: Moses says he controls only himself and his brother and asks God to separate them from the defiantly disobedient, the fracture of a community.
luna: The land is forbidden to them for forty years as they wander through the earth (يَتِيهُونَ فِي الْأَرْض), the explicit consequence of losing the route.

luna: Believers are told to seek a means of approach to God (الْوَسِيلَةَ) and strive in His way, naming the route of nearness. | terra: Believers are told to seek the means of approach to God and strive in His way ("سَبِيلِهِ").
terra: The Torah contains guidance and light, carried by prophets, rabbis, and scholars as a received route of judgement.
terra: The Gospel confirms the Torah and contains guidance and light for the God-conscious.

luna: Each community is given a law and a way (شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجًا); the passage preserves plurality while telling them to race in good deeds. | terra: Each community receives a law and a way ("شِرْعَةًۭ وَمِنْهَاجًۭا"); distinct rites remain answerable to one God rather than mere scattering.
terra: The messenger is told to judge by revelation and beware lest people turn him away from part of what God sent down.
terra: Jesus says, "ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبَّكُمْ", the same worship-address that 3:51, 19:36, and 43:64 call the straight road.

luna: People are warned against desires of those who went astray, misled many, and left the middle of the way (سَوَاءَ السَّبِيل). | terra: A prior people went astray, led many astray, and wandered from the level way ("سَوَآءِ ٱلسَّبِيل").

luna: God makes the Sacred House a standing support for people and a place of safety, alongside the sacred months and offerings. | terra: The Kaʿbah, the Sacred House, is made a "قِيَٰمًۭا لِّلنَّاس"—a standing support for people—beside the root of uprightness.

luna: People prefer the inherited track (مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا) over what God revealed, even when their fathers knew no guidance. | terra: Appeal to revelation is met by "what we found our fathers upon," even if the fathers knew nothing and were unguided.
terra: If believers are guided, those who go astray cannot harm them; responsibility for walking the course is personal.
terra: Jesus reports that he told his people to worship God, his Lord and their Lord, and was a witness while among them.
luna: Travel through the land and see the end of those who denied the signs, treating the earth as a record of prior travelers.
terra: The Prophet's grief is answered by the fact that, if God willed, He could gather all people upon guidance.

luna: Some are placed on a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), while others are left in layered darkness, a direct split between finding and losing the way. | terra: God may leave one in error or set one upon a straight road, making the two outcomes stand together.
terra: Signs are detailed so that the way of the criminals ("سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ") may become distinct.
terra: The Prophet is forbidden to worship those invoked apart from God and refuses to follow their desires lest he be among the straying.

luna: A bewildered person in open country (حَيْرَانَ) is called toward guidance (الْهُدَى) by companions waiting on the path. | terra: The lost person is bewildered on earth ("فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ حَيْرَانَ") while companions call him back "إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى".
terra: Those who believe without mixing faith with wrongdoing have security and are the guided.
terra: Abraham's family line is named as one God guided, beginning the sequence whose guidance the Prophet must follow.
terra: A further chain of prophets is named as righteous, thickening the human company of the road.
terra: More ancestors, descendants, and brothers are selected above the worlds, extending the guided line.

luna: The chosen forebears and descendants are guided to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), a line of favored predecessors. | terra: Chosen kin, descendants, and brothers are guided "إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ".

luna: God calls this direction His guidance (هُدَى اللَّهِ) and commands the Prophet to follow the guided predecessors. | terra: The guidance of the prophetic line would be nullified by association, marking worship's boundary.
terra: The same line receives Book, judgement, and prophethood, the provisions by which a people can be led.

luna: The Prophet is told to follow the guidance (هُدَاهُم) of the earlier prophets, an explicit line of predecessors. | terra: After naming the prophetic line, the Prophet is told, "فَبِهُدَىٰهُمُ ٱقْتَدِهْ"—walk after their guidance.
terra: Dawn, night-rest, sun, and moon are set for calculation, the celestial order immediately before the star-guidance of 6:97.

luna: Stars (النُّجُوم) orient travelers in land and sea at night; they are signs for people who know how to read them. | terra: Stars are made so people may find their way through the darknesses of land and sea ("لِتَهْتَدُوا۟").
terra: God, creator and guardian of all things, is named as the one to worship: "فَٱعْبُدُوهُ".

luna: Following most people would lead away from God's way (سَبِيلِ اللَّه), since they follow conjecture rather than a marked route. | terra: Following the majority on earth would lead one away from God's way because they follow conjecture.
terra: The Lord knows best who strays from His way and who are guided.

luna: The constricted chest of one turned away is likened to climbing into the sky, a bodily contrast before the Lord's straight path is named. | terra: Guidance opens the breast to Islam, while misguidance constricts it as though climbing into the sky.

luna: The Lord calls this straight path (صِرَاطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيمًا) and says it is made clear for those who remember. | terra: "وَهَٰذَا صِرَٰطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيمًۭا" follows detailed signs: the road is legible because its signs have been set out.
terra: Those who kill children and forbid provision without knowledge have strayed and are not guided.

luna: People are forbidden to follow Satan's footsteps (خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَان), a repeated trail leading away from God's route. | terra: Cattle include animals for carrying loads ("حَمُولَة") and animals close to the ground, provisioning human movement while warning against Satan's footsteps.
terra: God's conclusive argument includes the assertion that, if He willed, He could guide everyone together.
luna: The command to weigh with a just balance (الْمِيزَانَ بِالْقِسْطِ) stands among the teachings immediately before the one-path instruction.

luna: The Lord names one straight path (صِرَاطِي) and forbids the plural paths (السُّبُل) that divide its walkers. | terra: God names His own straight road, commands following it, and opposes the many "ٱلسُّبُل" that scatter walkers from it.
luna: The Book given to Moses is a completion, clarification, guidance, and mercy, continuing the preceding instruction about God's path.

luna: This blessed Book is sent down so people may follow it (فَاتَّبِعُوهُ) and be mindful, continuing the path stated in the preceding verse. | terra: The blessed Book is to be followed ("فَٱتَّبِعُوهُ") and feared, a scriptural road-command beside 6:153.
terra: The Book's descent prevents later people from claiming that scripture was limited to earlier groups, continuing the guidance passage of 6:155–157.
terra: A clear proof, guidance, and mercy have come from the Lord; turning away from these signs is the opposite response.
terra: Those who split religion and become sects are disowned by the Prophet; divided religious paths oppose one road.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to say that his Lord guided him to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), a steadfast religion (دِينًا قِيَمًا). | terra: "هَدَىٰنِى" joins "صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ" to "دِينًۭا قِيَمًۭا"; guided road, uprightness, and lived religion meet in one sentence.

luna: Iblis vows to sit in ambush on God's straight path (صِرَاطَكَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ), making the traveled route contested ground. | terra: Iblīs vows to sit in ambush on God's straight road, "صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ".

luna: Iblis describes attacking from every direction—front, back, right, and left—around the straight route. | terra: The ambush spreads from before, behind, right, and left, making the straight line's surrounding exposure visible.
terra: God tells Iblīs that Hell will be filled with him and those who follow him, closing the road-ambush passage.
luna: Satan and his tribe see humans while humans do not see them; the warning not to follow Satan's footsteps preserves the hidden ambush on the path.
terra: God commands justice, setting faces upright at every mosque, and sincere religion: bodily orientation, worship, and dīn are joined.

luna: One group is guided and another earns error; some take devils as allies while thinking themselves guided. | terra: One group is guided while error rightly falls on another that took devils as patrons and thinks itself guided.
terra: Messengers from among the people recite signs; guarding oneself and setting matters right becomes the response to their leading.
terra: The people of the Garden confess that they would never have been guided without God guiding them.

luna: The wrongdoers bar people from God's way (سَبِيلِ اللَّه) and seek to make it crooked, while denying the Hereafter. | terra: Wrongdoers bar people from God's way and seek crookedness in it ("عِوَجًۭا").
terra: A Book detailed with knowledge is brought to the people as guidance and mercy for believers.
terra: Noah tells his people to worship God alone, beginning the recurring prophetic way-call.
terra: Hūd tells ʿĀd to worship God alone, repeating the single-direction summons.
terra: Hūd's people resist leaving what their fathers worshipped, setting ancestral attachment against his single-God call.
terra: Ṣāliḥ tells Thamūd to worship God alone and brings them a sign from their Lord.
terra: Shuʿayb tells Madyan to worship God alone before his later prohibition on road-blocking.

luna: The people are forbidden to sit on every road (بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ) to threaten travelers and bar them from God's way (سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ). | terra: Shuʿayb forbids sitting at every road ("بِكُلِّ صِرَٰطٍ") to threaten, bar believers from God's way, and seek crookedness in it.
terra: After crossing the sea, Israel comes upon a people devoted to idols and asks for a god like theirs, a detour immediately after rescue.

luna: Those who turn arrogant from God's signs refuse the path of right guidance (سَبِيلَ الرُّشْد) and choose the path of error (سَبِيلَ الْغَيِّ). | terra: The arrogant refuse the way of right ("سَبِيلَ ٱلرُّشْد") yet take the way of error ("سَبِيلَ ٱلْغَىّ").

luna: Those who follow the Messenger find him described in earlier scripture and follow the light sent with him. | terra: The Prophet commands what is right, forbids wrong, relieves burdens, and is to be followed; those who follow him prosper.

luna: The Prophet is told to announce his universal mission and command belief in God and following him (فَاتَّبِعُوهُ) so people may be guided. | terra: All people are called to believe in God and His messenger and follow him "لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ".

luna: Among Moses's people is a community that guides by truth (يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ) and judges justly, a faithful group within a divided people. | terra: Among Moses' people is a community that guides by truth and judges by it.
terra: The Children of Israel are cut up through the earth into communities, a dispersed people beside the image of one travelled way.

luna: Whom God guides is truly guided, and whom He leaves astray are the losers, preserving both readings of the journey. | terra: Whom God guides is the rightly guided; those He leaves astray are the losers.

luna: Among God's creation is a community that guides by truth (يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ) and acts justly, preserving the presence of a rightly directed company. | terra: Among those created is a community that guides by truth and establishes justice through it.
terra: Whomever God leaves astray has no guide, and is left wandering in rebellion.
terra: Calling idols to guidance does not make them follow; inert objects cannot be the advancing guide.
terra: The Qur'an is called insights from the Lord, guidance, and mercy for a people who believe.
luna: Believers are called to what gives them life when God and the Messenger call them, a response to the guide's summons.
terra: Disbelievers spend wealth to bar people from God's way; their spending becomes regret before they are overcome.
terra: Those who leave their homes boastfully and bar from God's way display public movement that opposes the guided procession.
terra: Those who maintain God's mosques through faith, prayer, alms, and fear of God are hoped to be among the guided.
terra: God does not guide wrongdoing people even when they pride themselves on service around the sacred House.
luna: People who prefer family, wealth, trade, and homes over God, His Messenger, and striving in His way are warned of a rival attachment that displaces the path.
terra: The messenger is sent with guidance and the religion of truth for its manifesting over other religions.
terra: Some religious authorities consume wealth falsely and bar people from God's way ("عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ").
terra: The fixed number of sacred months is called "ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ", an upright, ordered religious time-course.
terra: Manipulating the sacred months is made fair to disbelievers and leads them astray; they make lawful what God forbade.
luna: Believing men and women are allies who command right, establish prayer, and obey God and His Messenger; God will show them mercy.

luna: The first forerunners among emigrants and helpers, and those who follow them well, form a favored succession of walkers. | terra: The first forerunners and those who follow them in goodness form a visibly preceding company whose route others take up.
luna: The believing community is characterized by repentance, worship, praise, devotion, command of right, and guarding God's limits, a practiced way of life.
terra: God does not let a people go astray after guiding them until He makes clear what they should guard against.
terra: Every thirst, fatigue, hunger, footfall ("مَوْطِئًۭا"), and gain from an enemy in God's way is written as a righteous deed.
terra: Every small or great expenditure and every valley crossed is recorded for those travelling in God's cause.
luna: Some from each community are to learn religion and return to warn their people, keeping guidance moving from one group to the next.
terra: Sun and moon are given light and measured phases so people know years and reckoning, furnishing ordered celestial signs.

luna: Believers are guided by their faith (يَهْدِيهِمْ رَبُّهُم بِإِيمَانِهِمْ) toward gardens beneath which rivers flow. | terra: Faith guides believers through their faith; rivers run beneath their gardens as the arrival of that course.
terra: People were one community and then differed; God's decisive word postpones judgement on their divided course.
luna: God calls people to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ). | terra: God calls to the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight road.
terra: After the truth, what remains but error; the question asks how people are turned away.

luna: The passage asks who guides to the truth (يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ) and who is more worthy to be followed, testing the guide as well as the route. | terra: The question contrasts one who cannot guide unless guided with God, who guides to truth: who deserves to be followed?
terra: The Qur'anic admonition is healing, mercy, and guidance for believers, an interior provision for the way.
terra: Moses asks about Pharaoh's given splendour and wealth through which people are led astray from God's way.
luna: Moses and Aaron are told to remain upright (فَاسْتَقِيمَا) and not follow the way of those who do not know.

luna: The Children of Israel cross the sea while Pharaoh and his forces pursue; drowning catches him as he claims belief too late. | terra: The Children of Israel cross the sea while Pharaoh pursues them in transgression and hostility, the anti-guide chasing the escaped way.
luna: Pharaoh is told that his belief comes only now after prior rebellion and corruption, when the route of return has closed.
luna: Pharaoh's body is preserved as a sign for later people, a trace left on the road of history.
terra: Israel is settled in a good place and provided for, yet later differs after knowledge comes to it.

luna: The Prophet says truth has come from the Lord; whoever accepts guidance does so for himself and whoever strays bears his own loss. | terra: Whoever is guided is guided for himself, and whoever strays does so against himself.
terra: A witness from God and Moses' Book as guide and mercy stand behind belief in the revealed route.
terra: Those who bar from God's way and seek crookedness in it are named as deniers of the final arrival.
terra: No counsel avails if God wills to leave a people in error; He is their Lord and return.
terra: Hūd says to ʿĀd, worship God; you have no god but Him, extending the prophets' shared worship-road.

luna: Hud says his Lord is on a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), presenting divine governance as the unwavering route. | terra: The Lord is "عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ" even in the scene of creatures held by their forelocks.
terra: Ṣāliḥ says to Thamūd, worship God; He produced you from earth and settled you in it.
terra: Shuʿayb says to Madyan, worship God; you have no god but Him, in the same mission that forbids road-blocking.
terra: Shuʿayb commands full measure and weight in justice and forbids corrupting the earth, the social practice beside his one-God call.
terra: Pharaoh is followed in this world and will precede his people into the Fire, completing the false-leader scene of 11:98.

luna: Pharaoh will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection to the Fire (فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ النَّارَ), a false guide taking a community to ruin. | terra: Pharaoh goes before his people ("يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ") and leads them into the Fire: the anti-guide reaches an opposite water-place.

luna: The Prophet and those with him are commanded to remain steadfast (فَاسْتَقِمْ) as ordered, a daily continuation on the straight way. | terra: The Prophet and those who turn with him are commanded, "فَٱسْتَقِمْ كَمَآ أُمِرْتَ"—continue straight as commanded.
luna: They are told not to incline toward wrongdoers, lest the Fire touch them, guarding the course from a harmful pull.
terra: God could make people one community, yet they continue to differ, a boundary to the image of one communal way.
terra: Joseph follows the religion of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, a named inheritance before his account of upright religion.
terra: Exclusive worship is called "ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ", joining the daily religion to the upright course.
terra: "دِينِ ٱلْمَلِك" means the king's law or order, showing a different social sense of the root that can organize a people's course.

luna: The Prophet calls to God with insight and declares, “This is my way” (سَبِيلِي), along with whoever follows him. | terra: The Prophet says, "هَٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِى", and calls to God with those who follow him on clear seeing.
luna: The hearers are asked whether they have traveled the land and seen the end of earlier peoples, reading the path through its traces.
terra: The stories of earlier people are detail, guidance, and mercy for believing people, so predecessors become a narrated route.
terra: God spreads the earth, places firm mountains and rivers, and gives signs in alternating night and day.

luna: Every people has a guide (هَادٍ), distinguishing the one who warns from the guide who leads ahead. | terra: Every people has a guide ("هَادٍۢ"), placing the advancing guide in the Qur'an's account of communities.

luna: Some ask for a sign, but God leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back (مَنْ أَنَابَ), linking return to finding the way. | terra: God leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back.
terra: The verse recalls that, if God willed, He could guide all people, while the believers continue to meet the consequences of others' refusals.
terra: One God has left astray cannot be guided by another ("فَمَن يَهْدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ٱللَّهِ").
terra: The messenger says he is commanded to worship God and not associate anything with Him; to Him he calls and returns.

luna: The Book brings people from darkness to light by their Lord's leave, onto the path of the Mighty and Praiseworthy (صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ). | terra: The Book brings people from darkness to light, toward the road of the Mighty, the Praised.

luna: Those who prefer worldly life to the Hereafter turn others away from God's way (يَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّه), making desire an obstruction. | terra: Those who prefer the nearer life bar people from God's way and seek its crookedness ("عِوَجًۭا").

luna: Messengers speak in their people's language to make the message clear; God guides or leaves astray whom He wills. | terra: Every messenger speaks his people's language to make matters clear; God then leaves astray or guides whom He wills.
terra: Moses is sent to bring his people from darkness into light and remind them of God's days.
luna: The messengers ask why they would not rely on God when He has guided them to their ways (سُبُلَنَا), and promise patience on that course.
luna: The good word is likened to a tree with a firm root (أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ) and branches in the sky, an image of a practice that holds and bears fruit.
luna: The rooted tree gives its fruit at every season (كُلَّ حِينٍ), like a way sustained through repeated acts.
luna: The evil word is an uprooted tree with no stability (اجْتُثَّتْ مِن فَوْقِ الْأَرْضِ مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ), the opposite of a path worn firm by faithful walkers.

luna: God makes believers firm with the steadfast word (الْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ) in this life and the next, keeping them on their ground. | terra: God makes believers firm with the firm word in this life and the next, while wrongdoers are left astray.

luna: People set rivals up to lead others away from God's way (لِيُضِلُّوا عَن سَبِيلِهِ), redirecting walkers from their Lord. | terra: Rivals are set up with God in order to lead people away from His way.
terra: Abraham asks that the city around the House be made secure and that he and his children be kept from idol paths.
terra: Abraham says idols have led many people astray, contrasting a created companion with the true guide.
terra: Abraham settles descendants by the Sacred House so they establish prayer, asks hearts to incline there, and asks provision of fruits.
terra: Constellations are placed in the sky and adorned for observers: celestial marks accompany the explicit star-navigation of 6:97 and 16:16.
luna: Iblis vows to mislead all people (لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ), naming the rival guide's aim. | terra: Iblīs promises to make earthly things attractive and to mislead people all together.
luna: Iblis admits that God's sincere servants are outside his power, preserving a community that does not take his route.
luna: God answers, “This is a straight path to Me” (صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ), placing the route under divine claim. | terra: God calls the protected return to Him "صِرَٰطٌ عَلَىَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌۭ".

luna: God's servants are beyond Iblis's authority except those who follow the deviants (الْغَاوِينَ), marking the boundary between routes. | terra: God tells Iblīs that he has no authority over God's servants except those who follow him among the deviators.
terra: Hell is the promised meeting-place for all of Iblīs's followers.
terra: Hell has seven gates, with an apportioned group entering through each—an opposite branching of paths.
terra: Horses, mules, and donkeys are made for riding and adornment, furnishing the traveller with carried movement through the prepared earth.

luna: The straight direction of the way (قَصْدُ السَّبِيل) belongs to God, while some routes swerve (جَائِر); this preserves both destination and deviation. | terra: God takes responsibility for the direction of the path ("قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيل") while some routes are crooked ("جَآئِر").

luna: Night, day, sun, moon, and stars are made subject to human use as signs for people who reason, complementing the landscape's markers. | terra: Night, day, sun, moon, and stars are subjected by God's command and are signs for people who understand.

luna: Ships travel through the sea and people seek provision from it, extending the created landscape around the roads and stars. | terra: Ships plough through the subjected sea so people may seek God's bounty, a watery counterpart to made routes on land.

luna: Mountains, rivers, and roads (سُبُلًا) are placed on earth so people may find their way (تَهْتَدُونَ). | terra: Mountains, rivers, and "سُبُل" are set in the earth "لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ": a made landscape gives the traveller a way.

luna: Wayfinding marks (عَلَامَاتٍ) and stars (النَّجْم) give travelers signs by which to find direction (يَهْتَدُونَ). | terra: "عَلَٰمَٰت" and the star are explicit landmarks by which people "يَهْتَدُونَ".

luna: Every community receives a messenger calling it to worship God and shun false gods; some are guided and others deserve error. | terra: Every community receives a messenger commanding worship of God and avoidance of false powers; some are guided and some are overtaken by error.
terra: Even the Prophet's desire for their guidance cannot overcome God's leaving a people astray; they have no helpers.
terra: To God belongs the enduring religion ("ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِبًا"), bringing habitual persistence into the dīn-root.
terra: The Book is sent to clarify what people differ about and as guidance and mercy for believers.
terra: The bee is inspired to take houses in mountains, trees, and human structures: a creature is given both dwelling and directed practice.
terra: The bee is commanded to eat and follow the made-easy ways of its Lord ("سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًۭا"), then brings forth nourishing drink.
luna: The parable contrasts a powerless owned servant (عَبْدًا مَّمْلُوكًا) with one who spends from good provision, preparing the next verse's contrast with a just man on a straight path.
luna: The just man commands equity and is upon a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), while the mute servant is a burden to his master.

luna: The Book is sent as clarification, guidance (هُدًى), mercy, and good news for those who submit, a guide for every community. | terra: The Book is sent as clarification of everything and as guidance, mercy, and good news for those who submit.

luna: God could make humanity one community but lets some stray and guides others; every group is answerable for its practiced course. | terra: God could make people one community, but leaves astray or guides whom He wills, holding their choices accountable.
terra: The Holy Spirit brings revelation to make believers firm and as guidance and good news for those who submit.

luna: Abraham is called a whole community (أُمَّةً) in himself, devoted and upright, a single forerunner whose life becomes a way to follow. | terra: Abraham is an "أُمَّةًۭ", devoted to God and upright ("حَنِيفًۭا"), a single person who carries a community's direction.

luna: Abraham is grateful for blessings and is guided to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), explicitly tying favor to the exemplary route. | terra: Abraham is chosen and guided to a straight road, a predecessor whose course can be followed.

luna: The Prophet is told to follow Abraham's religion (مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ), a straight way linked to the exemplary guide just described. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to follow Abraham's upright religion, making an earlier walked course a present command.
terra: The messenger is commanded, "ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ", to call to the Lord's way with wisdom and beautiful counsel.

luna: God takes His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque to show him signs, a guided journey between sanctuaries. | terra: The night journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque frames worship between two marked destinations.
luna: The Qur'an guides to what is most upright (أَقْوَمُ), naming revelation as the sign that straightens a walk. | terra: The Qur'an guides to what is more upright ("لِلَّتِى هِىَ أَقْوَمُ").
terra: Night and day are made two signs so people seek bounty and know the number of years and reckoning.

luna: Whoever is guided benefits himself, and no bearer carries another's burden, locating responsibility in each walker's steps. | terra: Whoever follows guidance does so for himself; no bearer carries another's burden, and punishment follows a sent messenger.
luna: Every people is called with its leader (بِإِمَامِهِمْ), showing a community's way and its guide brought into judgment.
luna: One who seeks the Hereafter and strives as a believer has effort acknowledged, preserving the route chosen toward the lasting home.
terra: Give full measure and weigh with the straight balance ("ٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ"), a material image of straightness.
terra: Do not walk on earth exultantly: walking cannot pierce the earth or reach the mountains in height.
terra: The Lord drives ships through the sea so people seek His bounty, carrying travellers across an otherwise impassable expanse.
terra: On the Day every people is called with its leader ("بِإِمَٰمِهِمْ"), making communal following visible at arrival.

luna: Whoever is blind to guidance here will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way (أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا). | terra: Whoever is blind in this world is blind in the next and farther astray in path ("أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًۭا").
terra: Each acts according to his manner, while God knows who is better guided in way ("أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًۭا").

luna: Whom God guides is rightly guided, and whom He leaves astray has no protector; they are gathered blind, mute, and deaf. | terra: Whom God guides is guided, and none can serve as protective guides for those He leaves astray.
terra: Even recitation is to seek a "سَبِيلًا" between loudness and secrecy: the middle of two extremes becomes a worshipful way.
terra: The Book is sent down with no crookedness in it ("عِوَجًۭا"), giving textual revelation the straightness of the requested road.
terra: The Book is "قَيِّمًۭا"—upright—so as to warn and give good news, carrying the q-w-m family into revelation itself.
terra: The youths ask their Lord to grant mercy and prepare for them right guidance in their affair ("رَشَدًۭا").
terra: The young people believe in their Lord, and God increases them in guidance.
terra: Leaving their people for the cave, the youths are promised mercy and a prepared ease in their affair.

luna: The sleepers' cave is described by the sun's course; the verse then says whom God guides is rightly guided and whom He leaves astray has no protecting guide. | terra: Whom God guides is guided, and for whom He leaves astray no directing patron can be found.
terra: The speaker asks that the Lord guide him to what is nearer than this in right conduct ("رَشَدًۭا").
luna: The Prophet is told to stay with those who call their Lord morning and evening and not follow a heedless heart's desire, a daily community of walkers.
luna: Iblis and his descendants are taken as allies instead of God, a choice of the rival company that once refused the command.
terra: After guidance comes, people are held back by the demand for an earlier destructive pattern or visible punishment.
terra: Turning away when reminded of God's signs makes a person unable to be guided ever.

luna: Moses says he will continue traveling until he reaches the meeting of the seas, setting out to seek knowledge. | terra: Moses sets out until the junction of the two seas, a journey whose destination must be found.

luna: The fish slips into the sea by a remarkable passage (سَرَبًا), a sign at the travelers' meeting place. | terra: At the junction the fish takes its way ("سَبِيلَهُ") into the sea, becoming the missed sign on the route.

luna: Moses asks for their meal after the journey has worn them out (نَصَبًا), a bodily detail of the path. | terra: After passing the junction, Moses asks for food because the journey has brought fatigue.

luna: The servant explains how the fish took its way into the sea (اتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ), making a sign into a direction. | terra: The attendant remembers the forgotten fish and its wondrous way into the sea, restoring the lost landmark.

luna: Moses recognizes the sign as what they were seeking, and they retrace their steps (فَارْتَدَّا عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمَا). | terra: "ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ"; they retrace their footprints ("ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًۭا") to the sought sign.

luna: They find a servant whom God gave mercy and taught knowledge, the guide at the end of their search. | terra: They find the servant given mercy and knowledge from God, the guide whom their retracing reaches.

luna: Moses asks to follow the servant of God so he may learn right guidance (رُشْدًا), making the learner seek a guide ahead of him. | terra: Moses asks, "هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ", to be taught what the servant has been taught of right guidance.
luna: The servant warns Moses he will not be able to remain patient with him, the trial of following a guide whose path is not yet understood.
luna: Moses is told he cannot encompass the servant's knowledge, a limit on the traveler's sight.
luna: Moses promises patience and obedience, the learner's commitment to follow the guide.
luna: The servant sets a condition: do not ask until he explains, ordering the learner's steps.
luna: Moses follows the knowledgeable servant by ship; the servant damages it, beginning the next stage of a journey whose sign Moses cannot yet read.
luna: The servant reminds Moses that he said he could not remain patient, testing the traveler's commitment to follow.
luna: Moses asks not to be taken to task for forgetfulness, continuing the learner's effort to stay on the route.
luna: They travel onward and meet a boy whom the servant kills, an act whose meaning remains hidden from the companion.
luna: The servant again recalls his warning about Moses's patience, marking another boundary in the following.
luna: Moses promises that if he asks again, the servant may leave him, accepting the consequences of failing to follow.
luna: They reach a town whose people refuse hospitality; the servant repairs a collapsing wall, the third sign encountered on the road.
luna: The servant announces their parting and promises to explain what Moses could not patiently witness.
luna: The damaged ship belongs to poor people who work at sea; the mark protects their livelihood from a king seizing every sound vessel.
luna: The boy's parents are believers, and the servant fears the boy would drive them into rebellion and disbelief.
luna: God intends to replace the boy with one better in purity and nearer in affection, preserving the parents' way.
luna: The repaired wall belongs to two orphans and hides their treasure; their righteous father and God's mercy preserve their inheritance until they mature.
luna: The Prophet is asked about Dhu al-Qarnayn, introducing another traveler whose route and signs unfold in the passage.
luna: God establishes Dhu al-Qarnayn in the land and gives him a means (سَبَبًا) to every matter, equipping a traveler to follow routes.
luna: Dhu al-Qarnayn follows a means (فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا), the repeated image of taking a way toward each destination.
luna: He reaches the setting of the sun and encounters a people there, a marked limit of his westward journey.
luna: He is told to punish the wrongdoer or treat the believer well, a judgment encountered at the edge of the route.
luna: The believer who does right receives the best reward and an easy command, a fitting course for those who accept guidance.
luna: Dhu al-Qarnayn follows another means (ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا), continuing from one direction to the next.
luna: He reaches the rising of the sun and finds a people with no shelter from it, another distinct region on the journey.
luna: God encompasses all that is with the traveler in knowledge, framing the journey and its people under divine sight.
luna: He follows yet another means (ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا), moving toward a third encounter.
luna: He reaches the space between two barriers and finds a people who can barely understand speech, a traveler arriving at a boundary.
luna: The people ask Dhu al-Qarnayn to build a barrier against Gog and Magog, seeking protection for their community.
luna: He asks them to help with strength and offers to build a barrier, making their shared work a defense along the way.
luna: Iron is brought and the gap is filled with molten copper, a physical boundary that stops passage.
luna: Gog and Magog can neither scale nor pierce the barrier, the route held against those who would cross it.
luna: Dhu al-Qarnayn calls the barrier mercy from his Lord and says it will be leveled when God's promise comes, preserving the boundary's temporary nature.
luna: The greatest losers are those whose effort went astray while they thought they were doing good (ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ), a path misread from within.
luna: Jesus again joins worship of God (اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ) to the straight way (صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ). | terra: Jesus repeats that shared lordship and worship are the straight road.
terra: The parties differ among themselves over Jesus immediately after his declaration of the straight road.

luna: Abraham invites his father to follow him and says God will guide him to a straight path (صِرَاطًا سَوِيًّا). | terra: Abraham asks his father to follow him so he may guide him to a level road ("صِرَٰطًۭا سَوِيًّۭا").

luna: The prophets are those God guided and favored; when the signs are recited they fall in prostration, exemplars along the path. | terra: The prophets are those God has favoured; when His signs are recited they fall prostrate and weeping.

luna: Later successors neglect prayer and follow desires (اتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَوَات), meeting ruin instead of the prophets' way. | terra: A later generation neglects prayer and follows desire, meeting "غَيًّۭا"—the contrary of the sustained worship-course.
terra: The Lord of heavens and earth is to be worshipped, and the worshipper is told to persist patiently in His worship ("وَٱصْطَبِرْ لِعِبَٰدَتِهِ").

luna: God increases guidance for those already guided (زَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ هُدًى), and enduring good works are better in reward. | terra: God increases those who are guided in guidance, while enduring good deeds remain better in return and outcome.
terra: God's self-disclosure to Moses commands worship and the establishment of prayer for remembrance.
terra: Moses and Aaron carry the message that peace is for whoever follows guidance.

luna: Moses says God gave each thing its form and then guided it (هَدَىٰ), extending wayfinding to every creature's fitting course. | terra: Moses describes the Lord who gives every thing its creation and then guides it ("ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ").
terra: Moses says his Lord neither errs nor forgets ("لَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَنسَى"), distinguishing divine unfailing knowledge from the traveller's lostness.

luna: God spreads the earth as a cradle and makes roads (سُبُلًا) through it so people may be guided (تَهْتَدُوا). | terra: The One who spreads the earth makes paths in it ("سُبُلًۭا") and sends water: a traversable ground is also provided for.
luna: People are told to eat and pasture their cattle in the earth's provision; signs in the land continue the road scene.
luna: People come from earth, return to it, and are brought out again, placing the traveled life inside a larger passage.
terra: Pharaoh's magicians fear that Moses and Aaron will drive them from their land and take away their ideal way ("طَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ").

luna: God tells Moses to travel by night with His servants and strike a dry path through the sea (طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا), without fearing pursuit. | terra: Moses is told to make for the servants a dry road in the sea ("طَرِيقًۭا فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَسًۭا").
luna: Pharaoh pursues them with his forces, then the sea overwhelms him, completing the false leader's route to destruction.
luna: Pharaoh led his people astray (أَضَلَّ قَوْمَهُ) and did not guide them (وَمَا هَدَىٰ), the false herdsman of a community.
luna: God is forgiving to whoever repents, believes, does right, and then remains guided (اهْتَدَىٰ), depicting a return to the path.
terra: In Moses' absence the Sāmirī leads his people astray, another counterfeit guide inside a guided community.
terra: Asked about the mountains, the messenger says the Lord will scatter them as dust, beginning the level-ground scene.
terra: After the mountains are scattered, God leaves the earth a smooth level plain ("قَاعًۭا صَفْصَفًۭا").
terra: The levelled earth will show neither crookedness nor unevenness ("لَا عِوَجًۭا وَلَآ أَمْتًۭا").
terra: On that day people follow the Caller with no crookedness for him ("لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥ"): a single unbending procession behind a guide.

luna: Whoever follows God's guidance will not go astray or be wretched, while turning from the reminder has the contrary end. | terra: Whoever follows God's guidance will neither go astray ("يَضِلُّ") nor be wretched.
luna: Turning away from God's reminder brings a constricted life and blindness on the Day of Resurrection, the lost traveler's outcome.

luna: The closing challenge asks which group is more guided and whose way is more right (أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًا), leaving the route open to judgment. | terra: The ending promises that the companions of the level road ("ٱلصِّرَٰطِ ٱلسَّوِىِّ") and the guided will become known.

luna: Every messenger is told that there is no god but God, so worship Him alone, a repeated foundation of the prophets' route. | terra: Every messenger receives the same revelation: no god but God, so worship Him.

luna: God sets firm mountains and makes broad passes (فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا) through the earth so people may find their way. | terra: God makes broad mountain passes, "فِجَاجًۭا سُبُلًۭا", so that people may be guided.
luna: Isaac and Jacob are given to Abraham, setting up the family of leaders who guide by God's command in the next verse.

luna: Abraham's family is made leaders guiding by God's command (أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا), a community that leads ahead. | terra: Abraham's line is made leaders who guide by God's command; worship, prayer, and almsgiving are revealed as their carried practice.
terra: "إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ" joins one community, one Lord, and the command "فَٱعْبُدُونِ".
terra: The one community cuts its affair into pieces among itself, though all return to God.
terra: Whoever takes Satan as patron is led astray by him and then "guided" to the punishment of the Blaze, a deliberately inverted guide.
terra: One disputes about God without knowledge, guidance, or an illuminating book.

luna: The arrogant turns aside to mislead others from God's way (لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّه), the counter-motion to guidance. | terra: Turning proudly, he leads others away from God's way and receives disgrace.
terra: One who worships God on an edge ("عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ") turns on his face when tested, the unstable opposite of steadfast walking.
terra: The revealed verses are clear signs; God guides whom He wills.
luna: Believers are guided to good speech and to the path of the Praiseworthy (صِرَاطِ الْحَمِيد). | terra: Believers are guided to good speech and to the road of the Praised ("صِرَٰطِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ").
luna: Some bar people from God's way and from the Sacred Mosque (يَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ), placing an obstruction on both route and destination.

luna: God appoints the House for Abraham and commands its purification for those who circle, stand, bow, and prostrate, defining the destination's practices. | terra: Abraham is shown the site of the House and commanded to purify it for worshippers, placing worship at the destination of a shown way.

luna: Abraham is commanded to call people to pilgrimage; they come on foot and on lean camels from every deep pass (كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ), converging from distant roads. | terra: The pilgrimage call brings people on foot and on lean mounts from every deep mountain track ("فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ").

luna: Pilgrims witness benefits and remember God's name over the cattle He provides, joining the journey to gratitude. | terra: Pilgrims witness benefits, name God over provided animals, eat, and feed the distressed poor.

luna: Pilgrims fulfill vows, end their rites, and circle the Ancient House, completing the route to its home. | terra: Pilgrims complete rites, fulfil vows, and circle the ancient House, extending the arrival scene of 22:26–27.
terra: Honouring God's ritual signs ("شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّه") makes landmarks an expression of hearts' reverence.

luna: Those given knowledge know revelation is truth from their Lord, and God guides believers to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ). | terra: Faith in the revealed truth is followed by God's guidance to a straight road.

luna: Every community has a rite to follow (مَنسَكًا هُمْ نَاسِكُوهُ), preserving differences in practice while calling the Prophet to his Lord. | terra: The messenger is affirmed to be upon straight guidance ("هُدًۭى مُّسْتَقِيمٍ") amid competing rites.
luna: Believers are told to bow, prostrate, worship their Lord, and do good, the embodied service immediately before the command to hold fast to Him.

luna: Believers are told to strive for God, follow Abraham's religion, hold fast to Him, and keep prayer; He is their patron and the best patron. | terra: Believers are told to strive for God, hold fast to Him, and live the religion of their father Abraham.
terra: On livestock and ships people are carried, joining animal and vessel to traversing a created world.
terra: Noah is sent to his people with the command to worship God alone, establishing the prophetic road before later messengers.
terra: A messenger among a later people repeats the command to worship God alone and fear Him.
terra: The communities of the prophets are one community ("أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ") under one Lord.
terra: People cut their common affair into factions, each group rejoicing in its separate share.
luna: The Prophet says he calls people to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), making the call itself a path forward. | terra: The messenger calls the hearers to a straight road.

luna: Those who do not believe in the Hereafter turn away from the path (الصِّرَاطِ), showing how a destination shapes direction. | terra: Those who do not believe in the hereafter are deviating from the road ("عَنِ ٱلصِّرَٰطِ لَنَٰكِبُونَ").
luna: Believers are told not to follow Satan's footsteps (خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَان), whose trail commands indecency and wrong.

luna: God guides to His light whom He wills; the parable of the lamp makes direction visible in darkness. | terra: God's light guides whom He wills to His light; the lamp image supplies an interior landmark for the traveller.
terra: Creatures made from water move on belly, two legs, or four; created locomotion varies within God's will.
luna: Clear signs are sent, and God guides whom He wills to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ). | terra: Clear verses are sent down, and God guides whom He wills to a straight road.

luna: Obeying God and the Messenger is followed by guidance (تَهْتَدُوا), joining listening to walking rightly. | terra: Obedience to the messenger is followed by "تَهْتَدُوا۟", making his delivered message the lead to follow.
luna: On the Day of Gathering, the worshipped are asked whether they led God's servants astray or whether the servants themselves strayed from the way (ضَلُّوا السَّبِيل).

luna: Every prophet faces enemies among criminals, while God is enough as guide (هَادِيًا) and helper. | terra: For every prophet there is an enemy, yet the Lord is sufficient as guide ("هَادِيًۭا") and helper.
luna: Those gathered on their faces toward Hell are the worst in position and furthest astray from the way (أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا).
terra: The idolaters say the messenger nearly led them away from their gods; the competing claims reveal a contest of guides.
terra: Many hear and reason no better than cattle; they are farther astray in way ("أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًۭا").

luna: The Prophet asks no wage except that a person may take a way to his Lord (سَبِيلًا), naming the response as a chosen route. | terra: The messenger asks no wage except that whoever wills take a path to his Lord ("سَبِيلًا").

luna: The servants of the Merciful walk gently upon earth (يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا), making their manner of walking an ethical sign. | terra: Servants of the Merciful walk humbly on earth, making bodily walking an enacted disposition.
terra: The servants of the Merciful neither squander nor withhold, but keep spending as a balanced "قَوَامًۭا".
luna: The faithful pray to be made leaders for the mindful (إِمَامًا), asking to become exemplars others can follow.
terra: Moses calls his earlier act one done while "ضَالِّين"—error in conduct rather than the literal lost traveller, widening the root's sense.

luna: God commands Moses to travel by night with His servants (فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي), beginning the journey out of Pharaoh's rule. | terra: Moses is inspired to travel by night with God's servants, beginning the sea-crossing procession.
luna: Pharaoh sends gatherers through the cities, mobilizing pursuit behind the travelers.
luna: Pharaoh calls the Children of Israel a small band, dismissing the community fleeing his rule.
luna: He says they have provoked his anger, naming the hostility behind the pursuit.
luna: Pharaoh's forces are described as numerous and alert, the threat following the travelers.
luna: The pursuers leave gardens and springs behind, the settled abundance they will lose.
luna: They leave fields, noble dwellings, and comforts, a trace of what the failed route abandons.
luna: God gives these places to another people, the destination and inheritance of the exodus.
luna: Pharaoh's forces catch up at sunrise, closing the distance on the travelers.
luna: The two groups see one another, and Moses's companions say they have been overtaken.

luna: Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him (سَيَهْدِينِ) as the sea and pursuing army close in. | terra: At the sea with the pursuers near, Moses says, "إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ".

luna: Moses is told to strike the sea; it parts into a dry path (طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا) for his people to cross. | terra: At Moses' strike the sea parts and each part becomes like a great mountain, continuing the dry-road scene of the exodus.
luna: The pursuing army is brought near the sea, following the same way into its end.
luna: Moses and all who are with him are saved, the guide and his community brought through.
luna: The pursuing others are drowned, the contrary end of the path they chose.
luna: This passage is made a sign, though most people do not believe, leaving a marker for later readers.
luna: Abraham says his Lord created him and guides him (يَهْدِينِ), an exemplary wayfinder's confession.
terra: The condemned confess they were in manifest error when they made equals with the Lord of the worlds.
terra: They say none led them astray except the criminals, naming false human guidance.
terra: Weigh with the straight balance ("بِٱلْقِسْطَاسِ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمِ"), making uprightness a just measure in Shuʿayb's moral road.
terra: The Qur'an is guidance and good news for believers.
terra: Those who deny the hereafter have their deeds made attractive and wander blindly ("يَعْمَهُونَ").

luna: The Queen's people are barred from God's way (فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيل), their worship misdirected by Satan's beautification. | terra: Satan makes the people's work fair and bars them from the way ("عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيل"), leaving them unguided.

luna: God makes the earth a stable dwelling, sets rivers and mountains within it, and separates the seas, the landscape around the traveler's way. | terra: God makes earth stable, rivers, and firm mountains, the terrestrial scene immediately before the navigation of 27:63.

luna: God guides people through land and sea darkness and sends winds as good news; the question is who makes a traveler find the way. | terra: God guides through the darknesses of land and sea and sends winds before mercy; navigation becomes a sign of divine leading.

luna: The Prophet cannot guide the blind out of their error (ضَلَالَتِهِمْ); only those who believe in God's signs will hear. | terra: The messenger cannot guide the blind away from their error ("عَن ضَلَٰلَتِهِم").

luna: Moses, traveling toward Midian, asks God to guide him to the middle of the way (سَوَاءَ السَّبِيل), matching the path's center and the lost traveler's prayer. | terra: Moses, travelling toward Madyan, asks to be guided to "سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيل"—the middle or right course of the road.
luna: At the water of Midian, Moses finds two women holding back their flock while shepherds water theirs, continuing his journey toward a new home.
luna: Moses waters the women's flock, withdraws to shade, and asks God for any good provision, a traveler acting generously while seeking refuge.
luna: One of the women comes walking modestly to invite Moses to meet her father, extending the route from the well to a household.
luna: The daughter describes Moses as strong and trustworthy (الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ), the qualities of a dependable guide and keeper.
luna: Moses is offered a household and a period of service, turning the traveler's arrival into an enduring place in a community.
luna: Moses confirms the agreed term, closing the journey sequence with a fulfilled pledge.
luna: After finishing his term, Moses travels with his family and sees a fire from the mountain's side, continuing the journey begun toward Midian.
luna: Pharaoh's chiefs are made leaders calling to the Fire (أَئِمَّةً يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّار), a guide-community turned toward ruin.
terra: Moses is given the Book after earlier generations, as insights for people, guidance, and mercy.

luna: Following desire without God's guidance is called greater error (أَضَلُّ), exposing an attractive but unmarked route. | terra: Who is more astray than one who follows desire without guidance from God?
luna: The Prophet cannot guide whom he loves; God guides whom He wills and knows best those ready to be guided. | terra: The Prophet cannot guide whom he loves; God knows those open to guidance.
terra: The fear of being snatched from the land if guidance is followed is answered by the secure sanctuary and provision God gives.
terra: Abraham tells his people to worship God and fear Him; that is better for them if they know.
terra: Shuʿayb is sent to Madyan with the recurring command to worship God and hope for the Last Day.
luna: Ad and Thamud are led astray by Satan after he beautifies their deeds and bars them from the way (السَّبِيل), though they had insight.
terra: The shared God of Muslims and People of the Book gives a common direction within a disputed religious landscape.
luna: God's earth is spacious, so believers are told to worship Him alone wherever they are (فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ), carrying service along the road.
terra: The secure sanctuary is contrasted with people being snatched away around it, answering fear of following guidance with a held destination.

luna: Those who strive for God are guided to His many ways (سُبُلَنَا), while God remains with those who do good. | terra: Those who strive for God are guided to "سُبُلَنَا"—His plural ways—under His companionship.
luna: People are told to travel the land and see the traces and end of earlier communities, reading the consequences left along the way.

luna: Those who follow desire without knowledge are left astray; no one can guide the person God leaves in error. | terra: Those who wrong follow desires without knowledge; none can guide one God leaves astray.

luna: The upright religion (الدِّينُ الْقَيِّم) is aligned with the human nature God created, naming a way of life that does not bend from its fit. | terra: Set the face toward the upright religion ("ٱلدِّينِ ٱلْقَيِّمِ"), the enduring fitting of human nature.
terra: Turning back to God, fearing Him, and establishing prayer provide the habitual orientation of the road.
terra: Associators split their religion and become sects, each party pleased with its own route.
luna: Travel through the land and see how earlier peoples ended, including the traces of their choices.
terra: Set the face toward the upright religion before the inescapable Day, preserving directedness toward a final arrival.

luna: The Prophet cannot guide the blind from their error (ضَلَالَتِهِمْ); only those who believe the signs will hear and submit. | terra: The messenger cannot guide the blind away from their error; only those who hear the signs can be led.

luna: The Qur'an is guidance (هُدًى) and mercy for those who do good, beginning the portrait of people who are on their Lord's direction. | terra: The Book's verses are guidance and mercy for those who do good.

luna: They establish prayer, give alms, and are certain of the Hereafter, practices that fill out the guided life described next. | terra: Those doers establish prayer, give alms, and are certain of the hereafter, the sustained practices of the guided.
luna: Such people are upon guidance from their Lord (هُدًى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ) and are successful. | terra: Those who establish worship and give alms are upon guidance from their Lord.
terra: God casts firm mountains into earth, scatters creatures through it, and sends water that grows every noble pair.

luna: Even when parents call to association, one must not obey but should follow the way of those who turn to God (سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّ). | terra: Even while keeping parental kindness, the believer is told to follow the way of the one who turns to God ("سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَىَّ").
terra: Do not turn the cheek in contempt or walk exultantly on earth; a travelled way has an ethic of posture.

luna: The instruction to be moderate in walking (وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ) and lower one's voice gives the path a measured gait. | terra: Be moderate in walking ("وَٱقْصِدْ فِى مَشْيِكَ"), a literal command to take the middle of one's gait.
terra: Submitting one's face to God while doing good grasps the firmest handhold, the secure attachment of the traveller.
terra: Moses is given the Book as guidance for the Children of Israel, immediately before leaders are made to guide by God's command.

luna: Leaders who guide by God's command (أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا) emerge through patience and certainty. | terra: Patient, certain people from Israel are made leaders ("أَئِمَّةًۭ") who guide by God's command.
terra: God speaks truth and guides to the way ("يَهْدِى ٱلسَّبِيلَ").

luna: The Messenger is presented as a beautiful pattern (أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ) for those who hope in God and the Last Day, a model whose footsteps can be followed. | terra: The messenger is an excellent pattern for one who hopes in God and the Last Day, a human model to walk after.

luna: People say they followed their chiefs and were turned away from the way (السَّبِيلَا), preserving the danger of walking behind the wrong guide. | terra: The condemned say they obeyed masters and great ones who led them away from the road.
luna: Believers are commanded to speak upright words (قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا), language that points straight rather than turning aside.

luna: God promises to set their deeds right and forgive them, showing upright speech shaping the walk and its destination. | terra: Obedience to God and messenger is called a great attainment, the practical following implied by guidance.

luna: Those given knowledge see revelation as truth that guides to the path of the Mighty and Praiseworthy (صِرَاطِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيد). | terra: Those given knowledge see that revelation guides to the road of the Mighty, the Praised ("صِرَٰطِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ").

luna: God measures travel between settled towns (قَدَّرْنَا فِيهَا السَّيْرَ), making a network of known stages through the landscape. | terra: Visible towns and measured stages are placed between a people and blessed towns: travel is made secure by a chain of landmarks.
luna: The travelers ask for longer distances (بَاعِدْ بَيْنَ أَسْفَارِنَا) and are scattered, turning a safe route into a judgment on a community.
terra: The two opposing parties are presented as either upon guidance or in manifest error, without allowing both courses to be true.
terra: At judgement the arrogant ask the weakened whether they barred them from guidance after it came; the answer exposes chosen following.
terra: The weakened reply that the arrogant plotted by night and day, commanding disbelief and rivals; their following was cultivated.

luna: The Prophet says misguidance harms himself and guidance comes through what his Lord reveals, keeping wayfinding dependent on revelation. | terra: If the messenger goes astray it is against himself, but his guidance comes by what his Lord reveals.

luna: One whose evil deeds are made attractive and seem good is contrasted with the guided; God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. | terra: God lets whom He wills go astray and guides whom He wills; ugly work can appear beautiful to its walker.
luna: The inheritors of the Book divide into those who wrong themselves, those moderate, and those who race ahead in good, preserving parallel walks within one inheritance.
luna: People are asked to travel through the land and see the end of those before them, whose greater power did not save them.
terra: The addressee is affirmed as one of the messengers: a guide is placed before a people.
luna: The Qur'an says the Messenger is on a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), the way embodied by the guide. | terra: The messenger is explicitly "عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ".
luna: A man comes running from the far side of the city and urges people to follow messengers who ask no wage and are rightly guided (مُهْتَدُونَ).
terra: The believing man says that taking other gods would put him in manifest error ("ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍ").

luna: The criminals are ordered to separate (امْتَازُوا) before the route of worship and the route of error are named. | terra: At the dividing Day the criminals are told, "ٱمْتَٰزُوا۟ ٱلْيَوْمَ"—separate yourselves—before the worship-and-path address resumes.

luna: The covenant forbids worshipping Satan (اعْبُدُوا الشَّيْطَانَ), the rival guide who diverts people from the straight way. | terra: The covenant with Adam's children forbids worshipping Satan, the rival who turns walkers from their road.

luna: God says to worship Him (اعْبُدُونِي): this is the straight path (صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ), joining service to the route itself. | terra: "وَأَنِ ٱعْبُدُونِى ۚ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ" explicitly identifies worship with the straight path.

luna: Satan has led (أَضَلَّ) many people astray from that path, making the counter-route visible. | terra: Satan has led a great multitude astray ("أَضَلَّ ... جِبِلًّۭا كَثِيرًۭا") immediately after the path-command.
luna: The destination of the diverted route is identified as the Hell they were promised (تُوعَدُونَ). | terra: This is the Hell promised to the people, the arrival beyond the opposite road.
