luna: They are told to enter and burn in that destination (اصْلَوْهَا), completing the way from misguidance to its end. | terra: They are commanded to enter it that day because of their disbelief.
luna: God could erase people's sight so they would race toward the path (الصِّرَاط), yet would they truly see where they were going?
luna: God could immobilize them where they stand so they could neither go forward nor return, the loss of all direction.
terra: Cattle are made subject to people, so some become their rides and some their food.

luna: The wrongdoers, their companions, and what they worshipped are gathered before being directed to the path of Hell in the next verse. | terra: The wrongdoers, their paired companions, and what they worshipped are gathered before being directed toward Hell's road.

luna: The condemned are to be guided (فَاهْدُوهُمْ) to the path of Hell (صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيم), where guidance leads to the contrary destination. | terra: The command "فَٱهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطِ ٱلْجَحِيمِ" keeps guidance and road but reverses their destination.
terra: "وَقِفُوهُمْ" halts those directed to Hell for questioning, making the opposite procession pause on its way.
terra: The condemned found their fathers astray, so they rush after their traces ("ءَاثَٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ").
terra: Their hurrying after the fathers continues the scene of inherited misdirection.
terra: Most of the earlier peoples went astray before the present people, extending the long history of lost tracks.

luna: Abraham says he is going to his Lord and expects Him to guide him (سَيَهْدِينِ), a traveler trusting the guide ahead. | terra: Abraham sets out, saying, "إِنِّى ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ"—a traveller whose destination and guide are the Lord.
luna: Moses and Aaron are guided to the straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), continuing the prophets' line of guides.
luna: The disputants ask David to guide them to the middle of the way (سَوَاءِ الصِّرَاط), bringing the path's center into the Qur'an's own language.

luna: David is told to judge with truth and not follow desire lest it lead him astray from God's way (سَبِيلِ اللَّه). | terra: Following desire causes a ruler to stray from God's way ("سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ"), contrasting straight judgement with an off-course will.
terra: Iblīs swears by God's might that he will mislead them all.
terra: The exception is God's devoted servants, the walkers protected from the false guide.
terra: God answers with the truth and declares what He says of the deceiver's end.
terra: Hell will be filled with Iblīs and all who follow him, the destination of that counter-route.
terra: The Book's sender commands, "فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصًۭا لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ".
terra: Pure religion is offered to God alone; worship's direction cannot be divided among mediators.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to worship God with religion sincerely His.
terra: The Prophet announces that he worships God with his religion sincere for Him.

luna: The guided are those who listen and follow the best of what they hear (فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُ), discerning which voice to walk behind. | terra: Those who listen to speech and follow its best are the ones God has guided and endowed with understanding.

luna: An opened heart for Islam is a light from the Lord; a hardened heart is in manifest error, contrasting readiness to receive the route. | terra: A breast opened to Islam stands upon light from its Lord, an inwardly illuminated course.

luna: The best teaching is sent down as a repeated Book; skins and hearts soften to God's reminder, which is His guidance (هُدَى اللَّه). | terra: God sends the best discourse; by it He guides whom He wills, while none can guide one He leaves astray.
terra: Whomever God leaves astray has no guide, despite others' attempts to frighten the believer with rivals.

luna: Whoever God guides cannot be led astray (مَن يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِن مُّضِلٍّ), securing the guide's authority. | terra: Whomever God guides cannot be misled, grounding the road's security in divine agency.
luna: The Book is sent with truth for people; whoever accepts guidance does so for himself and whoever strays bears his own loss.
luna: People are told to turn to their Lord and submit before punishment comes, a return to the way before the final destination.
luna: They are told to follow the best of what was revealed (اتَّبِعُوا أَحْسَنَ مَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم), a clear instruction for choosing the guide.
luna: Disbelievers are driven in groups to Hell, where its gates open; the wrong route has a collective destination.
luna: Those mindful of God are led in groups to the Garden; the two processions show opposing roads and ends.
luna: The people of the Garden praise God for fulfilling His promise and letting them inherit the land, the destination reached by the preceding procession.
luna: Travelers are asked to inspect the remains and fate of earlier peoples, reading the history written along the earth.
terra: God does not guide an extravagant liar, a moral obstruction to being led.

luna: Pharaoh claims, “I guide you only to the way of right conduct” (سَبِيلَ الرَّشَاد), though he leads toward ruin. | terra: The believing man warns Pharaoh's people that he fears for them a day of turning away, a direction reversed at judgement.

luna: On the Day of turning back, no one can protect the one God leaves astray (يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ), and there is no guide for him. | terra: On the day of turning away there is no protector; one God leaves astray has no guide.
terra: Joseph earlier brought clear proofs, yet persistent doubt later hardens into misdirection.
terra: Pharaoh's embellished work bars him from the way ("ٱلسَّبِيلِ"), immediately before the believing man's invitation to the path of rightness.

luna: The believing man answers with the same words—follow me and I will guide you to the way of right conduct (سَبِيلَ الرَّشَاد)—contesting Pharaoh's false direction. | terra: The believing man says, "ٱتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرَّشَادِ": follow me and I will guide you to the path of rightness.

luna: The believer says, “Why do I invite you to salvation while you invite me to the Fire?” making rival calls into opposed roads. | terra: The believing man asks why he calls his people to salvation while they call him to the Fire.
terra: He contrasts their invitation to disbelief and association with his invitation to the Mighty, Forgiving God.

luna: The false object of worship cannot answer a call; the return is to God and transgressors end in the Fire. | terra: The false call has no claim in this world or the next; all return to God, while the extravagant belong to the Fire.

luna: Moses is given guidance (الْهُدَىٰ) and the Children of Israel inherit the Book, continuing the line of revealed guides. | terra: Moses is given guidance and the Children of Israel inherit the Book, continuing the succession of guided communities.
luna: The Book is guidance (هُدًى) and a reminder for people of understanding, making memory part of remaining on the way.
terra: Livestock are made for riding and for food.
terra: Livestock carry needs in human breasts, while ships carry people as well.
luna: The same call to travel and see the end of earlier peoples turns the land into evidence for a walker's judgment.
terra: The messenger calls to one God, then commands, "فَٱسْتَقِيمُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِ" and seek forgiveness.
terra: God fixes mountains, blesses the earth, and measures its provisions ("قَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقْوَٰتَهَا").

luna: Thamud are shown guidance, yet choose blindness over it (اسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَىٰ عَلَى الْهُدَى), an explicit refusal of the marked way. | terra: Thamūd are shown guidance but prefer blindness to guidance, choosing an anti-direction.

luna: Those who say God is their Lord and remain steadfast (اسْتَقَامُوا) receive angels and the promise of the Garden. | terra: Those who say their Lord is God and then remain straight ("ٱسْتَقَٰمُوا۟") receive the angels' reassurance.
terra: The finest speech calls to God, acts rightly, and declares submission; it supplies a voiced invitation onto the course.
luna: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs; people are told to worship their Creator rather than the celestial markers that orient them.
terra: The Qur'an is guidance and healing for believers, while its call remains deafness and blindness to others.

luna: The same religion is prescribed to Noah and later messengers; people are told to establish it and not divide over it. | terra: One religion is ordained to Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad; the later split is contrasted with that shared course.
terra: People divide only after knowledge has come to them, out of mutual transgression.

luna: The Prophet is told to stand firm as commanded (فَاسْتَقِمْ) and not follow their desires, a direct instruction to keep the straight course. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to call, remain straight as commanded, and not follow their desires amid religious dispute.
terra: Partners invent a religion not authorized by God, an unauthorized path-making beside the ordained religion.
luna: Ships on the sea are likened to mountains (كَالْأَعْلَامِ), the root's mountain-markers rising as navigational signs.

luna: One whom God leaves astray has no protector after Him and, seeing punishment, asks to return to the world, when the route is already closed. | terra: Whomever God leaves astray has no protecting guide afterward.
terra: The wrongdoers have no protectors to help them against God, and no way out is available.

luna: Revelation is made a light by which people guide others, and the Prophet is told that he guides to a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ). | terra: The revealed spirit is made a light by which the messenger guides to a straight road.
luna: The straight path is identified as God's path (صِرَاطِ اللَّهِ), to whom belongs all in the heavens and earth.
luna: The same Lord created the heavens and earth, the setting for the roads and traveling signs in the next verses.

luna: The earth is made a resting place with roads (سُبُلًا) running through it for travelers to be guided. | terra: The earth is made a cradle and furnished with paths "لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ", a direct parallel to the prepared road.
luna: Rain revives dead earth after the roads are named; the passage moves from the traveler’s route to the sign of return.
terra: God makes all pairs and provides ships and cattle for riding, extending the made-path image to its means of travel.
terra: Riders settle upon the backs of their mounts and remember the Lord's favour in subjecting them.
terra: The rider confesses that all will return to the Lord, making each conveyed journey hear its final destination.

luna: People defend inherited religion by saying they found their fathers on a community (أُمَّةٍ) and follow their traces (آثَارِهِمْ), a path by habit rather than guidance. | terra: The people claim to find their fathers on a "أُمَّة" and follow their tracks, an inherited path that may be unexamined.

luna: The same inherited-trace argument is repeated by earlier communities whenever a warner comes, showing how an old track can resist a guide. | terra: Each town repeats the claim that it follows ancestors' tracks ("ءَاثَٰرِهِم"), contrasting following revelation with following footprints alone.
luna: The messenger asks whether he has brought better guidance than the ancestral way; they insist on following their fathers.
terra: Abraham rejects what people worship apart from the Creator, "فَإِنَّهُۥ سَيَهْدِينِ".

luna: Whoever turns away from the Reminder is assigned a devil as companion, who then bars him from the path in the next verse. | terra: Turning from the Merciful's reminder assigns a devil as a close companion, an alternative leader.

luna: Those turned from God's reminder by Satan think they are rightly guided (يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ), though he bars them from the path (السَّبِيل). | terra: Those companions bar people from the path ("عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيل") while the people think themselves guided.

luna: The Prophet is told to hold fast to what is revealed because he is on a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ). | terra: The messenger is told to hold fast to revelation because he is upon a straight road.
luna: The passage says not to doubt and to follow God; this is a straight path (صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ), while preserving the disputed reading around Jesus and the Hour.
luna: Jesus comes with clear proofs and commands fear of God and obedience, the lead-in to his straight-path statement.

luna: Jesus repeats that worship of God is the straight path (صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ), a parallel witness to the Fatiha's worship-path image. | terra: Jesus again joins "فَٱعْبُدُوهُ" to "هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ".
luna: The groups differ among themselves after Jesus' clear statement, turning the one straight way into dispute.

luna: Moses is commanded to travel by night with God's servants (فَأَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي), leading a community away from Pharaoh. | terra: Moses is told to set out by night with God's servants, the beginning of the sea-route escape.
terra: He is told to leave the sea still; Pharaoh's army will be drowned, completing the route's protected crossing.
terra: The Children of Israel differ only after knowledge comes to them, out of rivalry.

luna: The Prophet is set upon a revealed way of the matter (شَرِيعَةٍ) and commanded to follow it, not the desires of the ignorant. | terra: The Prophet is placed on a "شَرِيعَةٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْر" and told to follow it rather than the desires of the unknowing.
terra: Those who wrong cannot avail one another against God; their mutual following cannot replace divine guardianship.
terra: The Qur'an is insight for people, guidance, and mercy for a people of certainty.

luna: One who makes desire his god is left to hearing and sight sealed, a self-directed route that mistakes appetite for a guide. | terra: Following one's own desire as god leaves a person astray despite knowledge, with hearing and sight sealed against direction.

luna: Those who say God is their Lord and then remain steadfast (اسْتَقَامُوا) have no fear or grief. | terra: Confessing God as Lord and then standing straight removes fear and grief, like following received guidance.
luna: They are the companions of the Garden, abiding there as reward for what they did, completing the steadfast path's end.

luna: The jinn say the revealed Book guides to truth and a straight path (صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ), making them fellow travelers who recognize the sign. | terra: The Qur'an confirms earlier revelation and guides to truth and a straight road.

luna: Those who disbelieve and bar others from God's way (صَدُّوا عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّه) have their deeds made fruitless. | terra: Those who disbelieve and bar people from God's way have their deeds made lost ("أَضَلَّ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ").
terra: Belief in the revelation to Muhammad brings forgiveness and reform of condition, the repair promised to the guided.
terra: God will guide the believers and set their condition right, the promised continuation after struggle.
luna: People are told to travel the land and see the fate of those before them, the route bearing visible traces of prior choices.
luna: One who stands upon clear proof from the Lord is contrasted with one whose evil conduct is made attractive, exposing two different ways of seeing.

luna: Those already guided are given increased guidance (زَادَهُمْ هُدًى), so the path deepens through continued attention. | terra: Those who have accepted guidance receive an increase in guidance and their God-consciousness.

luna: Those who turn back after guidance are led by Satan and given false hopes, abandoning the route after it was shown. | terra: Those who turn back after guidance becomes clear are drawn by Satan's false promises.

luna: Those who disbelieve and bar others from God's way (صَدُّوا عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّه) obstruct the route for other walkers. | terra: Disbelieving, barring from God's way, and opposing the messenger after guidance is clear cannot harm God.

luna: The Prophet is promised guidance to a straight path (صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا), joined to forgiveness and divine favor. | terra: Forgiveness and completion of favour culminate in God's guidance of the Prophet to a straight road.
luna: After promising victory, God says He will guide the believers to a straight path (صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا), placing success inside guidance.
terra: The believers are promised entry into the Sacred Mosque in safety, the arrival at a protected House.

luna: God sends the Messenger with guidance (بِالْهُدَىٰ) and the religion of truth, preparing the portrait of his companions in the next verse. | terra: The messenger is sent with guidance and the religion of truth, the third formulation beside 9:33 and 61:9.
luna: The Companions' mark of prostration and likeness to a seed that strengthens and thickens portray a community growing through following.

luna: Faith is made beloved and disbelief hateful to the believers, and the verse names them as rightly guided (الرَّاشِدُون). | terra: Faith is made beloved and disbelief, rebellion, and disobedience hateful; such people are the rightly guided.
luna: That rightly guided state is described as grace and favor from God (فَضْلًا وَنِعْمَةً), linking the community to bestowed favor.
terra: God spreads the earth, casts in firm mountains, and grows every lovely pair as signs.
luna: The Garden is brought near to the mindful and is no longer far, the destination of the people who kept their course.
luna: The Garden is promised to every returning and watchful person (أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ), describing the practiced character of its walkers.
luna: Those who feared the Merciful unseen and came with a heart turned to Him are told to enter in peace.
terra: "فَفِرُّوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ" gives the hearer a decisive direction of flight toward God.

luna: Humans and jinn are created to worship God (لِيَعْبُدُونِ), giving the path of service a stated purpose. | terra: Jinn and humankind are created "لِيَعْبُدُونِ", giving worship the final purpose beneath the road image.
terra: People follow conjecture and desire even though guidance has already come from their Lord.
luna: The Prophet is told to turn from one who turns away from God's remembrance and desires only the nearer life.

luna: That preference marks the limit of their knowledge; God knows best who has strayed from His way and who is guided. | terra: God knows best who strays from His way and who is guided, after desire and conjecture have been exposed.
terra: Thamūd reject following a single human messenger, saying that following him would put them in error and burning.
terra: The criminals are in error and burning, binding "ضَلَٰل" to the Fire's final outcome.

luna: The believers' light runs ahead of them and at their right (نُورُهُم يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ), like a sign lighting the road to the Garden. | terra: Believers' light runs before them and at their right, a leading illumination at the moment of arrival.
terra: The hypocrites ask believers to wait for their light, but are told to turn back behind them and seek a light there.
terra: Those who believe in God and His messengers are the truthful and witnesses with their Lord, a company already arrived by faith.
luna: Believers are told to race toward forgiveness and a Garden broad as heaven and earth, making the walk urgent and its destination clear.

luna: God gives believers a light by which they walk (نُورًا تَمْشُونَ بِهِ), making guidance visible underfoot. | terra: Faith gives a double mercy and a light by which believers walk ("تَمْشُونَ بِهِۦ").
luna: Satan's party forgets God and becomes the losing party, a community following a rival guide.
luna: Those with faith written in their hearts are God's party, set against Satan's party as two loyalties and destinations.
luna: The emigrants who left homes for God's favor and help form the first community of the path.
luna: The Helpers love those who migrated and prefer them over themselves, preserving the conduct of a community that receives later walkers.
luna: Believers are told to look at what they have sent ahead for tomorrow (قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ), making each day's steps matter at the destination.
luna: Those who forget God forget themselves; they are the rebellious, losing their orientation and their own way.

luna: Abraham and those with him are presented as a model in disavowing false worship and turning to God, though the passage preserves the limits of that example. | terra: Abraham and those with him are given as an excellent model, a predecessor-community to take as a pattern.
terra: That Abrahamic company is an excellent model for those who hope in God and the Last Day.

luna: When Moses's people deviate (زَاغُوا), God lets their hearts deviate; persistent turning away hardens the direction. | terra: When people deviate ("زَاغُوٓا۟"), God turns their hearts; departure from the line becomes inward misdirection.
terra: God does not guide wrongdoing people who invent lies about Him.
terra: The messenger is sent with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion.
terra: The disciples answer Jesus' call as helpers of God; one group of Israel believes and another disbelieves, and believers are strengthened.
terra: A messenger among the unlettered recites signs, purifies, and teaches Book and wisdom to people once in manifest error.

luna: Whoever believes in God has the heart guided by Him (يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ), bringing inward direction into the image. | terra: Whoever believes in God, God guides his heart, locating a path's direction within the heart.
luna: For whoever is mindful of God, He makes a way out (مَخْرَجًا), an opening when the course is constrained.
luna: God provides from an unexpected source and is enough for whoever relies on Him, sustaining the route He opens.
terra: A messenger recites clear verses to bring believers from darkness into light.
terra: The repentant believers' light runs before them and at their right as they ask God to complete it for them.
terra: Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion ("ٱلْمُلْك"); the sovereign sense of the Mālik-root frames the later tamed earth of 67:15.
terra: The people of the Fire admit that a warner came, but they denied and called the warning a great error.

luna: The earth is made tame (ذَلُولًا) for people to walk its slopes and eat its provision, closely echoing the image of a beaten, subdued road. | terra: The earth is made "ذَلُولًۭا"—yielding underfoot—and people are told to walk its shoulders and eat its provision.

luna: The verse contrasts one who walks face down with one who walks upright on a straight path (سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ). | terra: The one walking fallen on his face is set against one walking upright ("سَوِيًّا") on a straight road: the bodily image of guidance is made explicit.

luna: The Lord knows best who has strayed from His way (سَبِيلِهِ) and who is guided (الْمُهْتَدِينَ), judging the competing routes. | terra: The Lord knows best who has strayed from His way and who are guided.
terra: Noah calls his people to worship God, be conscious of Him, and obey him.

luna: God makes the earth spread out (بِسَاطًا), immediately before describing its broad roads for travelers. | terra: God makes the earth a spread carpet ("بِسَاطًۭا"), the ground beneath a travelled way.
luna: The earth is spread out with broad roads (فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا) for people to travel along. | terra: The carpeted earth is for taking wide mountain roads, "سُبُلًۭا فِجَاجًۭا".
terra: The jinn hear a wondrous Qur'an that guides to rightness ("إِلَى ٱلرُّشْدِ").
terra: The jinn distinguish an evil intended for earth from a Lord intending right direction ("رَشَدًۭا").
terra: The jinn say, "كُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ قِدَدًۭا"—diverse, parted ways—an exact image of groups scattered across tracks.
terra: Those who submit seek right course ("تَحَرَّوْا۟ رَشَدًۭا").
terra: The unjust among the jinn become fuel for Hell, the counterpart to Muslims seeking right course.

luna: If people remain upright on the way (اسْتَقَامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ), God gives them abundant water, joining steadfastness to provision. | terra: Remaining straight on the way ("ٱسْتَقَٰمُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلطَّرِيقَةِ") is answered with abundant water, joining a maintained course to provision.
terra: The reminder lets whoever wills take a way to his Lord ("سَبِيلًا").
luna: Believers are told to recite what is easy, keep prayer, give alms, and send good ahead to find it with God, the repeated practices of a sustained path.
terra: God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills; the numbered guards become a test of reception.

luna: God shows the human being the way (هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيل), leaving him grateful or ungrateful, two responses after direction is made clear. | terra: God says, "إِنَّا هَدَيْنَٰهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ", then opens the two responses, grateful or ungrateful.
luna: The Qur'an is a reminder, and whoever wills may take a way to his Lord (اتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا). | terra: The reminder lets whoever wills take a path to his Lord.
luna: Human willing remains under God's will, preserving divine guidance alongside the traveler's choice.
terra: The earth is made a container gathering the living and the dead.
terra: It gathers the living and the dead together, the inhabited ground beneath all routes.
terra: Tall firm mountains and fresh water are placed in earth, provisioned features of its landscape.
terra: The earth is made a resting-bed, a further image of ground made fit beneath human movement.
terra: Mountains are made pegs, continuing the formed-landscape imagery that supports paths and landmarks.
terra: Moses is sent to Pharaoh with the invitation, "وَأَهْدِيَكَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَتَخْشَىٰ".
terra: After the heaven, God spreads out the earth ("دَحَىٰهَآ").
terra: He brings from it its water and pasture, provision beside the made ground.
terra: He fixes its mountains firmly.
terra: These are enjoyment for people and their grazing animals.
luna: The one who transgresses (طَغَىٰ) begins the contrary course described in the next verses.
luna: Preferring the nearer life (آثَرَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا) makes the path turn away from the lasting home.
luna: Hell is the destination of that preference (فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَىٰ).
luna: The one who fears standing before the Lord and restrains the soul from desire takes the opposing route.
luna: The Garden is the home of that restrained soul (فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَىٰ), the other destination.
luna: God makes the human's way easy (ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ), a bodily path from origin into life. | terra: After creating the human, God makes the way easy for him ("ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُۥ").
luna: The question “Where are you going?” (فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ) turns the hearer toward the direction of the Qur'an's reminder.
luna: The Qur'an is a reminder for all worlds, making the call to choose a way universal.

luna: Whoever wills among you may take a straight way (أَن يَسْتَقِيمَ), the explicit direction behind the question. | terra: The address is for whoever wills among people to go straight ("يَسْتَقِيمَ").
luna: People do not will except as God wills, holding human choice and divine guidance together.
luna: The human being toils toward his Lord (كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا) and will meet Him, a life-long walk to a destination.

luna: People are told they will move from stage to stage (طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍ), marking life as passage through successive conditions. | terra: Human beings will ride stage after stage ("لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍ"), a compressed image of successive passage.
luna: God creates and proportions (خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ), making the world fit before the next verse says He determines and guides.

luna: God determines and then guides (قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ), joining measured form to an assigned direction. | terra: The Creator proportioned, measured, and guided ("قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ"); guidance is fitting each thing to its course.
luna: The one who purifies himself (تَزَكَّىٰ) succeeds, an active course that bears good fruit.
luna: He remembers his Lord's name and prays, giving the purified path its repeated practice.
luna: People prefer the nearer life (تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا), choosing the short road over what lasts.
luna: The Hereafter is better and more lasting (خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ), naming the destination that endures.
terra: The raised mountains are offered for looking, a landmark in the visible world.
terra: The earth is offered for looking as it is spread out, a final panorama of traversable ground.
luna: God gives the human being two eyes, bodily signs that precede the verse about two conspicuous paths.
luna: The tongue and lips make speech possible, another gift before the way between good and evil is shown.

luna: God guides the human to two conspicuous heights or ways (النَّجْدَيْن), placing a choice between routes before him. | terra: The human being is shown the two high roads ("ٱلنَّجْدَيْنِ"), making guidance a choice of track.

luna: The hard ascent (الْعَقَبَة) is not taken, introducing the difficult but fitting route of service. | terra: The human has not yet taken the steep ascent ("ٱلْعَقَبَةَ"), making the chosen road demanding.

luna: The steep ascent is explained as a demanding passage, not a flat or effortless walk. | terra: The question "what will make you know the steep ascent?" pauses at the threshold of that moral route.
luna: Freeing a slave is the first act on the steep path (فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ). | terra: Freeing a slave is named as a passage through the ascent.
luna: Feeding on a day of hunger continues the difficult route of mercy. | terra: Feeding on a day of severe hunger is another act on the steep route.
luna: The hungry one is an orphan near of kin, giving the route a concrete vulnerable traveler. | terra: The food reaches an orphan close of kin, giving the hard path a concrete fellow traveller.
luna: The route reaches a poor person in dust (مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ). | terra: Or it reaches a poor person lying in dust, extending the road's ethics to the lowly.

luna: Those who take it join faith to mutual patience and mercy (تَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ). | terra: Then comes faith and mutual urging to patience and mercy: a community sustains the ascent together.
luna: The people of the right are the community who pass along that steep route (أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ).
luna: Those who disbelieve the signs are people of the left, the contrary community to those who complete the steep ascent.
luna: Fire closes over the people of the left, showing the far end of their chosen course.
luna: The soul is proportioned (سَوَّاهَا), recalling a made-fit form before its moral directions are described.
luna: The soul is shown its wickedness and its mindfulness (فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا), the inward signs of two possible routes.
luna: The one who purifies the soul succeeds (أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا), a practiced course bearing its result.
luna: The one who buries the soul fails (خَابَ مَن دَسَّاهَا), preserving the contrary outcome.
luna: Night covers and day shines, a recurring sign of alternation that frames the two courses in the following oath.
luna: The bright day is paired with the covered night before the passage distinguishes different human striving.
luna: The creation of male and female precedes the statement that people's efforts and paths differ.
luna: Human striving goes in different directions (إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ), preparing the opposed easy and hard routes.

luna: The one who gives and is mindful begins a repeated course of action that God will make easy toward ease (فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ). | terra: Giving, God-consciousness, and believing the best prepare a person for an eased course.
luna: Affirming the best (صَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ) is the conviction that accompanies the easy route. | terra: Believing "بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ" identifies the trust that precedes ease.

luna: God makes the generous person's way easy toward ease (لِلْيُسْرَىٰ), showing habit as ground made traversable. | terra: God promises, "فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ"—We will ease him toward ease.
luna: The one who withholds and feels self-sufficient begins the contrary course. | terra: Miserliness, self-sufficiency, and denial begin the contrary course.
luna: Denying the best (كَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ) marks the opposite belief and direction. | terra: Calling the best a lie turns away from the trust that makes a way easy.

luna: God makes that person's way easy toward hardship (لِلْعُسْرَىٰ), preserving the contrary reading of a path made easy in the wrong direction. | terra: God promises, "فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ"—easing toward hardship as the counter-course.
luna: When the miser falls, his wealth will not save him, the consequence of the hardship-bound course.
luna: Guidance itself rests with God (إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ), the ground of the two routes just described. | terra: God declares, "إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ"—guidance rests with Us.
luna: The Hereafter and this life belong to God, framing the two courses by their final destination.
luna: The Fire is warned of as the blazing destination (نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ) of the contrary course.
luna: Only the most wretched (الْأَشْقَى) enters that fire, identifying the one who rejects the way.
luna: The one who denies truth and turns away (كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ) is marked by refusal of the guidance.
luna: The most mindful is kept far from the Fire (وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَى), the saved walker's contrary end.
luna: He gives from his wealth to purify himself (يُؤْتِي مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّىٰ), continuing the giving course of the opening verses.
luna: His giving is not payment for a favor owed to anyone, preserving sincerity in the route.
luna: He gives only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High (ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَىٰ).
luna: He will be satisfied (وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ), the promised end of the purified course.
luna: God found the Prophet an orphan and gave him shelter, one of the favors surrounding the lost-and-guided verse.

luna: God finds the Prophet ضَالًّا and guides him (فَهَدَىٰ); this can mean one who had not found the way, as well as one astray. | terra: "وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلًّۭا فَهَدَىٰ" holds lostness and being led together in the compact reversal that closes Fātiḥah.

luna: God found the Prophet in need and enriched him, another bestowal (أَغْنَىٰ) beside the guidance of verse 7. | terra: The One who found the addressee lost and guided also found him needy and made him self-sufficient, joining direction to provision.
luna: The Prophet is commanded not to oppress the orphan, turning received favor into care for another traveler.
luna: He is told not to repel the one who asks, a concrete practice for those who have received guidance.

luna: He is told to proclaim the favor of his Lord (بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ), explicitly recalling the root in “those You favored.” | terra: The addressee is told to speak of his Lord's favour, a response to having been found and guided.
luna: When one task is finished, the Prophet is told to strive on (فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَانصَبْ), continuing the work without stopping on the road.
luna: He is told to turn his desire toward his Lord (وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَارْغَب), fixing the route's destination.
terra: Those given Scripture do not split apart until after clear evidence has come to them.

luna: People are commanded to worship God with sincere devotion, as an upright religion (الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمَة), joining sustained service to the straight way. | terra: People of scripture are commanded to worship God sincerely, establish prayer, and give alms; this is "دِينُ ٱلْقَيِّمَةِ".
luna: Those who believe and do good are called the best of creation (خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ), the community walking the upright religion.
luna: Their reward is gardens of lasting residence and God's pleasure, the end of the path of worship and sincerity.
luna: Whoever has done an atom's weight of good will see it, making every small step visible at judgment.
luna: Whoever has done an atom's weight of evil will see it too, preserving accountability for every contrary step.
luna: Time is sworn by as it passes, measuring the repeated ground on which the path is walked.
luna: Human beings are in loss except for the community of faith and good work, those who exchange truth and patience.
luna: Mutual counsel in truth and patience makes steadfast companions on the way rather than isolated walkers.
terra: The Quraysh are commanded to worship the Lord of this House after their journeys.
terra: The Lord of the House feeds them against hunger and makes them safe from fear, provision and safety at the journey's end.
terra: "ٱلدِّين" here is recompense or judgement, retaining the Fātiḥah word while changing the habitual-path nuance.

luna: The closing distinction “you have your religion and I have mine” (لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ) preserves divergent commitments and ways of life. | terra: "لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِىَ دِينِ" marks divergent religious courses without treating them as one shared path.
luna: People enter God's religion in crowds (يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا), a community gathering onto the way.
